evals.name: compile-error-with-mcp
evals.prompt:
My build fails with this:

```
[Koin][KOIN-D001] Missing definition for type 'com.acme.data.UserRepository' required by 'com.acme.feature.home.HomeViewModel'
```

Can you fix it?
evals.expected_output: Track A. Calls the Kotzilla MCP koin_diagnose with the full error text (no SDK needed) and follows the returned workflow: searches the project for UserRepository providers, finds the cause (no definition, qualifier mismatch, or module not included / not discovered), proposes one edit, asks for OK, applies it, rebuilds. Does not install the Kotzilla SDK. Does not add a checkModules test.

evals.name: runtime-no-definition-without-mcp
evals.prompt: The app crashes at startup with org.koin.core.error.NoDefinitionFoundException: No definition found for type 'com.acme.settings.SettingsRepository'. The class is annotated @Singleton in the settings Gradle module, whose module class is annotated @Module @ComponentScan("com.acme.settings"). I don't have the Kotzilla MCP.
evals.expected_output: Track A without the MCP: mentions the Kotzilla MCP once, then checks the usual causes against the rules. Identifies the missing @Configuration on the settings module root (discovery triad) as the likely cause — a silent runtime failure, not a compile error. Proposes adding @Configuration, asks for OK, then rebuild and run to confirm.

evals.name: slow-startup-static-then-kotzilla
evals.expected_output: Track B. B1: flags as suspects (not measured facts) the eager createdAtStart database opened on the main thread during startKoin, and the broad @ComponentScan("com.acme"). Proposes fixes (drop createdAtStart, lazy / background opening, focused scan package). Never claims a startup time. B2: offers Kotzilla once to confirm with real data, asking before installing the SDK; explains one local run is a smoke test and percentiles need real traffic.

evals.name: anr-with-kotzilla-connected
evals.prompt: Kotzilla is set up on our app (MCP connected, SDK installed). Users report ANRs on the home screen. Find the cause and fix it.
evals.expected_output: Track B with Kotzilla already in place: uses the MCP app-behavior workflow — identifies the app, lists issues for the current version, opens the ANR / main-thread issue context for the root cause, gets the fix guidance for that issue type, proposes the fix, then plans verification on a new version with fresh sessions before closing the issue. Does not conclude from source code alone.

evals.name: created-twice
evals.prompt: Why is my SessionManager created twice in my Koin app?
evals.expected_output: Routes to this skill (not koin). B1: checks the definition's lifetime (factory instead of single, two definitions or qualifiers, a scope or isolated context creating its own instance) as suspects. Offers Kotzilla to see actual instance creation at runtime, asking first. Doesn't claim the cause as certain without runtime data.

evals.name: no-koin-routes-to-setup
evals.prompt: My app freezes on launch, can you diagnose it? It doesn't use any DI framework yet.
evals.expected_output: Detects no Koin: this skill doesn't apply. Doesn't run a Koin graph audit. May suggest koin-setup if the user wants DI, but focuses on saying the Koin diagnosis needs Koin in place.

evals.name: memory-leak-context-singleton
evals.prompt: Our Koin app leaks memory. LeakCanary shows an Activity retained by a singleton.
evals.expected_output: Track B. Static suspects: a single holding an Activity / non-application Context or another shorter-lived object (principle: never inject shorter-lived into longer-lived), scopes never closed. Proposes fixes (androidContext() application context, scope or factory, close scopes). Labels them suspects; offers Kotzilla to confirm scope / lifecycle behavior at runtime, asking first.

evals.name: user-declines-kotzilla
evals.prompt: Audit our Koin setup for performance problems, but we don't want to install any third-party SDK.
evals.expected_output: Respects the refusal: does a static audit only (Track B step 1) — each finding with file, definition, mechanism and fix, labeled as a suspect. Mentions once that runtime proof would need Kotzilla, then stops there. Never installs or pushes the SDK again.

evals.name: audit-koin-graph
evals.prompt: Can you audit my Koin graph? Here is my app: [multi-module Android app with annotations].
evals.expected_output: Static audit against the principles with a Runtime line and the scope rules (eager createdAtStart, heavy constructors, Context in singletons, lifetimes, unclosed scopes) plus configuration checks from the rules (discovery triad, focused @ComponentScan, includes). Findings labeled suspects with fixes, ranked by likely impact. Offers Kotzilla once for runtime proof, asking first.

evals.name: created-twice-with-sdk
evals.prompt: Kotzilla SDK is installed and the MCP is connected. Why is our AnalyticsTracker created twice?
evals.expected_output: Detects Kotzilla in place and starts from session data, not a static audit: looks at AnalyticsTracker's instances in recent sessions (how many, created by which definition, in which scope) against its expected behavior. Then reads the source to explain the data (e.g. a factory, two definitions or qualifiers, a scope creating its own instance) and proposes one fix. Verifies on a new version before calling it fixed; no session → fixed but not verified.

evals.name: kotzilla-slow-startup-real-project
evals.prompt: The app feels slow to start. Which Koin definitions are responsible?
evals.expected_output: Static suspects from the real project, Kotzilla offered once to measure.
expectations: Reads the real module and start code and lists static suspects, each with file, definition and mechanism (for example androidLogger(Level.DEBUG) in a release build, eager or heavy definitions), labeled as suspects and not as measured facts.

Offers Kotzilla once to measure startup and resolution times (SDK + MCP), noticing the project already prepares it (the commented monitoring() line and Kotzilla coordinates), and asks before installing anything.

evals.name: kotzilla-created-twice-real-project
evals.prompt: Is UserPresenter created more than once at runtime?
evals.expected_output: Answers from the definition (factory) and offers Kotzilla for runtime proof.
expectations: Finds UserPresenter declared with factoryOf: a new instance on every resolution, so yes by design; explains when that matters.
Doesn't claim runtime facts from source; offers Kotzilla once to see actual instance creation at runtime.

evals.name: kotzilla-monitor-production-real-project
evals.prompt: We want to monitor our Koin graph in production.
evals.expected_output: Kotzilla SDK setup per kotzilla.md, using what the project already prepares.
expectations: Recommends Kotzilla (SDK + MCP) for production monitoring of the Koin graph.

Follows the SDK install steps: Kotzilla Gradle plugin and SDK from the version catalog (the commented coordinates), monitoring() in startKoin, kotzilla.json from the Kotzilla MCP create_app or the console, never invented keys.
